## Two-stage Miller op-amp with NMOS input pair and RC-nulled compensation

**Stage 1.** An NMOS differential pair (M1/M2) drives a PMOS current-mirror load (M3/M4). I chose an NMOS input because the PMOS threshold is about 1 V. With VCM = 0.9 V, a PMOS input would have no headroom.

**Stage 2.** A PMOS common-source device (M6) drives an NMOS current sink (M8). This gives a rail-to-rail-ish output that easily meets the 1.2 V swing requirement.

**Bias.** A diode-connected NMOS (MB) sinks the 10 µA reference from `ibias`. It is mirrored to the tail (M5, about 60 µA) and to the output sink (M8, about 300 µA). The current ratios are set by W5/WB and W8/WB, since M5 and M8 share LB.

**Compensation.** Cc runs from the first-stage output `y` to `vout`, in series with a nulling resistor Rc. Rc is set at or above 1/gm6 to push the right-half-plane zero into the left half plane.

**Polarity.** `vinn` drives the diode side (M1→M3), and `vinp` drives the mirror-output side (M2→M4). If vinp rises, node y falls, M6 conducts more, and vout rises. So vinp is the non-inverting input, as the testbench requires.

### Hand-sizing estimates

| Requirement | Hand calculation | Margin vs. spec |
|---|---|---|
| Power | (10 + 60 + 300) µA × 1.8 V ≈ 0.67 mW | under the 1 mW limit |
| Input-pair gm | gm1 ≈ 30 µA × 12 ≈ 360 µS | — |
| GBW | gm1 / (2π · 3 pF) ≈ 19 MHz | ≥ 10 MHz spec |
| Slew rate | min(60 µA / 3 pF, 300 µA / 13 pF) ≈ 20 V/µs | ≥ 10 MV/s spec |
| Phase margin | gm6 ≈ 3 mS vs. the 2.2·gm1·CL/Cc ≈ 2.6 mS rule | Rc adds further margin |
| DC gain | (~40 dB) × (~35 dB) ≈ 75 dB with L ≥ 0.5–1 µm | ≥ 70 dB spec |

```spice
.subckt dut vinp vinn vout vdd vss ibias
* ---- bias: sink IREF with diode-connected nfet ----
MB  ibias ibias vss vss nfet W={WB} L={LB}
* ---- tail current source ----
M5  tail  ibias vss vss nfet W={W5} L={LB}
* ---- input differential pair (vinn on diode side, vinp on output side) ----
M1  x   vinn tail vss nfet W={W1} L={L1}
M2  y   vinp tail vss nfet W={W1} L={L1}
* ---- PMOS current-mirror load ----
M3  x   x   vdd vdd pfet W={W3} L={L3}
M4  y   x   vdd vdd pfet W={W3} L={L3}
* ---- second stage: PMOS common source + NMOS sink ----
M6  vout y     vdd vdd pfet W={W6} L={L6}
M8  vout ibias vss vss nfet W={W8} L={LB}
* ---- Miller compensation with nulling resistor ----
Rc  y   cz  {Rc}
Cc  cz  vout {Cc}
.ends dut
```

```json
{"params": {
  "WB": [4, 1, 20],
  "LB": [1, 0.5, 4],
  "W5": [24, 4, 150],
  "W8": [120, 20, 800],
  "W1": [8, 2, 60],
  "L1": [0.5, 0.15, 2],
  "W3": [20, 2, 100],
  "L3": [1, 0.3, 3],
  "W6": [140, 20, 800],
  "L6": [0.5, 0.15, 2],
  "Rc": [1000, 100, 20000],
  "Cc": [3e-12, 0.5e-12, 10e-12]
}}
```

These are hand estimates only; nothing has been simulated, so the optimiser's SPICE runs will be the first real check against the specs.

### Notes for the optimiser

- **Systematic offset.** Ideally W6/L6 ≈ 10·W3/L3, so that the mirror and M6 currents match the 300 µA set by M8. The DC servo in the testbench absorbs any systematic offset, so TPE can trade this ratio freely.
- **Tail headroom.** At VCM = 0.9 V the tail node sits at about 0.15–0.2 V. The ranges therefore allow a wide, low-Vdsat W5 relative to WB.
- **Power control.** The power budget is set mainly by W8/WB, which fixes the second-stage current. TPE should keep W8/WB at or below about 35 to stay under 1 mW.
